# Manual orchestration

Every model call re-sends the caller's whole context; in the 2026-10-05 to 10-09 baseline about 73% of estimated quota spend was that re-send. Most rules in this skill either remove a call or lower what each call carries.

Use model judgment to divide an authorized objective into coherent outcomes whose evidence and ownership can be checked. Keep the accepted objective, authority, source identity, unresolved work and review requirements visible. Packet precision is not proof that all obligations were found; test the proposed decomposition against the owning contract and relevant boundaries before dispatch and when new facts appear. The route, slice size and order may change when evidence warrants it.

## Load by role

There are two levels. The supervisor is the top-level role (the root), and the user is its parent. It dispatches builders directly and launches reviewers separately; no coordinator sits above it and no supervisor sits between it and its workers.

- When forming or revising an organization, including during ongoing implementation with no new dispatch, launch or discovery assignment: [organization formation](references/organization-formation.md) - reviewable candidates, branch discovery and revision authority.

- **Supervisor** (top level): [supervisor](references/supervisor.md) - scope and budget, decomposition, packets, dispatch, validation, review collection, integration.
- **Worker or reviewer**: [worker](references/worker.md) - one coherent bounded assignment.
- **Every role**: [call cost](references/call-cost.md) - waiting, batching, request sizing.
- **Supervisor**: [context boundary](references/context-boundary.md) - retained or fresh before dispatch, transfer, roots. Workers carry their own mid-task check.
- When considering same-session context replacement: [same-session continuity](references/same-session-context.md) - authority, durable meaning, supported controls, visible resumption and recovery.
- **On Codex**, with any role: [Codex host](references/codex-host.md) - builder children, separate top-level reviewers, service tier and identity binding.
- **On Claude Code** (Anthropic models), with any role: [anthropic host](references/anthropic-host.md) - tool mapping, transcript-based context check.
- When launching, continuing or collecting a **Pi** role: [Pi host](references/pi-host.md) - API or subscription lane, per-launch service tier, turn observation, no-network container mode.
- After a run: [measurement](references/measurement.md). For a concrete artifact example: [demonstrated forms](references/demonstrated-forms.md).

Repository instructions and owning contracts still govern each role.

## Launching a child

At launch, give the child its packet and tell it to load this skill for its role: invoke `$manual-orchestration`, or read `skills/manual-orchestration/SKILL.md` in the repository when the skill is not installed. It loads its own references; do not paste this skill or other guidance documents into its brief.

After launch, verify the role's actual session ID and rollout from recorded lineage, using the host reference's lookup for its launch mechanism, then send its identity binding: session ID, rollout, parent/collection owner, continuation path, and the pinned context-status binary path and SHA-256. An ID cannot be verified before the session exists, and a role name or inherited `CODEX_THREAD_ID` can name another session. The role acknowledges the binding at its next boundary and records it in its continuation. For a retained role, deliver the binding explicitly once and expect it in the continuation thereafter.

## Invariants

Separate worker completion, unfinished continuation, acceptance of a bounded subject, private readiness, and integration; the supervisor makes the last three, and they remain separate decisions. Carry exact source, subject, binary/schema and evidence identity where those affect the claim; preserve failures and uncertainty. Refresh the *meaning* of affected claims when source or assumptions change, not just their hashes. Record requested model/effort separately from observed identity, and leave unavailable measurements unknown. The supervisor retains responsibility for collecting required child results and owned processes.

This is a manual coordination adapter. In a configured Slice Builder campaign, use its owning [skill and receipt contract](../slice-builder/SKILL.md) unless that contract's owner accepts compatible continuation semantics. An unfinished manual `handoff_ready` is not its terminal `audit_receipt`, `handoff_receipt`, or gate success. The skill grants no new mutation, provider, review, acceptance or publication authority.

## Deterministic outer host

The optional [manual host](references/manual-host.md) composes native Codex dispatch, owned observations, exact-turn collection and acknowledged receipts for an explicitly authorized objective. It leaves semantic decisions and existing domain records with their owners.

## Scripts

- `scripts/provision_manual_host.sh [repo]` - build and pin the optional Rust manual host with its compatible adapter bundle; no global activation.
- `scripts/provision_context_status.sh [repo]` - build and pin the context-status binary outside the shared target; prints path and SHA-256.
- `scripts/child_context.py` - `check` one Codex session, `tree` a parent's children, or `claude` a Claude Code subagent transcript against the trigger and observed compaction band; writes a record to retain.
- `scripts/role_host.py` - host a role or child as a Claude `--bg`, Codex app-server or Pi session: `launch` (with `--parent` to record it in the ledger), `status`, `deliver`, `retire`, `children`, `whoami`. Pi launches name a lane with `--auth api|subscription` and may set `--service-tier` on the api lane; `--container` runs each turn without network behind a host egress proxy (`scripts/pi_container.py`); see [Pi host](references/pi-host.md). Codex also supports `rename`, `archive`, and `unarchive` without a model turn, plus `settings --rollout` to observe applied model/effort/tier for continuation. Detects and stops a Claude copy-on-resume fork.
- `scripts/auto_continue.py` - bounded foreground same-SID compaction and attributed recovery; use under [same-session continuity](references/same-session-context.md#foreground-automatic-continuation-on-the-codex-app-server).
- `scripts/root_rotation.py` - root transfer gate: `prepare` publishes continuation lineage and stops at `awaiting_authority`; `commit` or `watch` checks that the handoff is still available, launches the successor, waits for its typed `adopt` and retires or keeps the predecessor. `--title` provides a readable task name. See [context boundary](references/context-boundary.md#roots).
- `scripts/custody.py` - `run` a build or test, or a plan of them, recording PIDs, wait status, output and input digests and leftover processes; `freeze` a tree outside the repository into a manifest, archive and baseline diff. See [worker](references/worker.md#builds-tests-and-frozen-subjects).
- `scripts/scope_budget.py` - original scope, additions, the objective's sessions and its cost limits in the assignment record; `check` reports spend and time and says whether to reconsider or stop. See [supervisor](references/supervisor.md#scope-and-budget).
- `scripts/handoff_validator.py` - checks a root handoff's referents (paths, path-bound digests, labelled git refs, placeholders): 0 pass, 21 defect, 32 not established.

1	# Running on Claude Code (Anthropic models)
2	
3	The role references are written in Codex terms. On Claude Code the roles,
4	packets, evidence rules and the retained-or-fresh decision are unchanged; the
5	mechanics map as below. Load this with your role reference when the session
6	is Claude Code.
7	
8	| Codex | Claude Code | difference that matters |
9	| --- | --- | --- |
10	| `spawn_agent`, `fork_turns="none"` | `Agent` tool with a non-fork `subagent_type` (`general-purpose`, or a narrower type when it fits) | A `fork` inherits your whole context; it is a retained context, not a fresh one. |
11	| `followup_task` | `SendMessage` to the agent's ID | **Any** message to a finished agent resumes it with its full transcript. Every `SendMessage` that carries work is a retained dispatch and needs the pre-dispatch check. |
12	| `wait_agent` | nothing: the harness notifies on completion. The child's result arrives separately, as a framed hand-back message (`SubagentHandback`); the completion notice carries no result text | Do not read or tail a running agent's output file, sleep, or list agents to check progress. Do independent work or end the turn's tool use until notified. |
13	| requested model and effort | `Agent` `model` (`opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`, `fable`) | Set `effort` only when the user or an owning instruction asks. Observed model is `message.model` in the transcript. |
14	| rollout, `session_meta` lineage | `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<root session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` and `agent-<id>.meta.json` | The ID is returned by the spawn call. `meta.json` records the description, tool-use ID, `agentType`, `parentAgentId`, `spawnDepth`, `requestShape`, and the requested `model` and `effort`. A nested child's files sit in the **root** session's `subagents/`, with `parentAgentId` naming its parent. The spawn result also names a `tasks/<id>.output` file; it is the full transcript, so do not read it. |
15	| shared worktree | `Agent` `isolation: "worktree"` | Use it when parallel builders could touch the same files; the worktree is removed if unchanged. **Check the base at entry:** two harness worktrees on 2026-10-22 started at `a69efc44`, 278 commits behind HEAD. The packet names the required base; the worker runs `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git status --short`, resets its own clean branch to the base if they differ, records it, and stops if the tree is dirty. |
16	
17	## Models and review tiers
18	
19	Model, effort and review-tier choices for this host live in
20	[model selection](../../../docs/model-selection.md) (the Claude-host rows). Pass the
21	choice through `Agent` `model` as above. That parameter takes an alias, so record
22	the observed exact identifier from `message.model`.

24	## Context check
25	
26	`<skill-dir>` is the manual-orchestration skill's directory.

28	```
29	python3 -I <skill-dir>/scripts/child_context.py \
30	  claude --transcript <subagents dir>/agent-<id>.jsonl \
31	  [--next-task-tokens <estimate>] --out <assignment dir>/context-check-N.json
32	```
33	
34	The pinned CLI gives the same reading plus accounting:
35	`<pinned binary> claude --transcript <path> [--json]` for one transcript, and
36	`<pinned binary> claude-agents --session <id> --with-usage [--json]` for every
37	subagent of a session (counts each `message.id` once with its maximum output,
38	and excludes a fork's inherited parent call).
39	
40	Context is input + cache-creation + cache-read tokens of the latest assistant
41	call. Transcripts record no window, so the levels are absolute and their basis
42	differs from Codex:
43	
44	- **Trigger 150,000** carries over on a cost basis only: every call re-sends
45	  the whole context, so a retained 160K child pays about six times a fresh
46	  child's ~25K opening on each call (Codex measurement; the Claude opening is
47	  `not established`). H1's status is unchanged: a pilot hypothesis.
48	- **Band floor 202,533** is the lowest of 20 Claude Code auto-compactions on
49	  this machine as of 2026-10-21 (median 302,526, max 968,704, mixed windows).
50	  It is a lower bound, not the window.
51

53	reading 163,367 without running this check, because the skill had no Claude
54	reader yet. The re-review completed; by H1 it should have been a fresh reviewer
55	or a recorded overrule (continuity of the reviewer's own findings is a valid
56	reason).

# Repository Instructions

Before working in this repository, read and follow [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md), the
binding doctrine for system design and architectural constraints. Treat it as
required context for all planning, implementation, review, and documentation work.

[PHILOSOPHY.md](PHILOSOPHY.md) explains why that doctrine exists and is
explicitly non-normative. Read it in full for design, architecture, planning,
and doctrine or instruction review, where its rationale shapes the result. For
bounded implementation, validation, and mechanical work, consult it when a
decision turns on that rationale. Context loaded at startup is re-sent with every
later model call, so startup context should be the binding doctrine plus what the
task needs ([PHILOSOPHY.md §17](PHILOSOPHY.md#17-the-role-of-the-design-document)).

## Pre-release compatibility policy
Work Engine is under active development. Internal implementations and
interfaces have no backward-compatibility guarantee unless an explicit consumer
or owner-approved contract requires one.  Prefer the simplest architecture that
satisfies current requirements and the intended system design.  Existing code
is reusable implementation material, not architectural authority. It may be
modified, replaced, or removed.  Preserve approved semantics, data integrity,
provenance, and qualification evidence—not obsolete implementation behavior.
Any recommendation to preserve compatibility must identify the specific
consumer, the consequence of breaking it, and the cost of maintaining it.  

## Model-selection guidance
[Model selection](docs/model-selection.md) provides current defaults and their
tradeoffs when choosing an engineering model. It is decision guidance, not an
override of explicit user choices or campaign/provider contracts; consult it
when that choice is in scope, rather than inferring a selection from inheritance.

## Rust development direction

[Rust development](docs/rust-development.md) records the user's Rust-first
direction for new first-party implementation and proposed shared-code boundaries.
Use it when choosing implementation language or reusable package placement;
existing components and their authority remain until accepted replacement.

## Where files go

Readers judge a file's standing from where it sits. Put a new file where
[repository layout](docs/repository-layout.md) says, and follow its rules when
moving or citing one.

## Coordinating sub-agents

Outside a configured Slice Builder campaign, a Codex or Claude Code session
that coordinates sub-agents, or that a parent launches under
[the manual-orchestration skill](skills/manual-orchestration/SKILL.md), uses
that skill and loads only the references it names for the active role. A
child launched under another skill or review contract follows that contract.

## Durable role schedules

Scheduled obligations can outlive model context, but a schedule does not create
authority or activate an agent. When a durable scheduler capability is
configured and this session has an active human-supervised role, read and
follow [the role-scheduler skill](skills/role-scheduler/SKILL.md) at startup.
Reconcile overdue, due, and near-term items before ordinary work that could make
them stale or invisible. Do not emulate durable scheduling by storing future
obligations only in model context or an unobserved terminal.

## Continuous Wind Walker

In the first turn of every new context window created by a session restart,
context reset, or compaction, invoke and follow `$wind-walker` before resuming
unfinished work. Perform this invocation in the new context window so the
skill governs recovery and continuation there.

Before intentionally replacing context, invoke `$wind-walker` and ensure all
continuation-critical objectives, authority boundaries, commitments,
unresolved obligations, and references have durable owners. If that cannot be
established, do not replace context.

If replacement occurs outside the agent's control, invoke `$wind-walker` in
the new context window and stop rather than continue when correct recovery
still depends on meaning lost with the prior context.

## Shared Codex coordination board

Concurrent Codex sessions share files but do not share conversation context.
At session startup, after compaction recovery, before claiming a shared
resource, and before any paid or externally consequential operation, read the
repository chatboard:

```bash
python3 skills/durable-state/scripts/codex_chatboard.py --repository . read --limit 20 --active-claims
```

This returns the newest messages and unexpired claims. When a task needs older
history, page forward with `--since <sequence>`.

Post concise transition messages for resource claims, launches, pauses,
interruptions, replacements, and terminal results. Include exact artifact or
campaign references. Use `claim` before operating on a shared campaign,
ordinal, reviewer episode, or publication resource, and `release` when done.
Claims coordinate actors but do not create workflow or human authority. The
board is CAS-published through private Git refs and does not modify a branch,
index, or working tree.

Command lines (generated from `--help`):

<!-- cli-synopsis script=skills/durable-state/scripts/codex_chatboard.py subs="post claim release read" display="python3 skills/durable-state/scripts/codex_chatboard.py --repository ." -->
```text
python3 skills/durable-state/scripts/codex_chatboard.py --repository . post --author AUTHOR --session-id SESSION_ID --topic TOPIC --body BODY [--message-id MESSAGE_ID] [--ref REF] [--wake] [--kind KIND] [--role ROLE] [--to TO] [--reply-to IN_REPLY_TO] [--supersedes SUPERSEDES] [--effects-file EFFECTS_FILE] [--data-file DATA_FILE]
python3 skills/durable-state/scripts/codex_chatboard.py --repository . claim --resource RESOURCE --author AUTHOR --session-id SESSION_ID --note NOTE [--claim-id CLAIM_ID] [--ttl-seconds TTL_SECONDS]
python3 skills/durable-state/scripts/codex_chatboard.py --repository . release --resource RESOURCE --session-id SESSION_ID --claim-id CLAIM_ID
python3 skills/durable-state/scripts/codex_chatboard.py --repository . read [--since SINCE] [--limit LIMIT] [--active-claims] [--kind KINDS] [--role ROLES] [--format {json,compact}]
# other subcommands (put --help after one for its usage): wait, topics, roles, requests, handoff-publish, handoff-status, owner-boundary-io, kinds, adopt
```
